title: Sixteen Miles and One Turned Signpost
subtitle: 方向与指引 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 方向与指引（生活与学习·方向与指引）
meta: 主题语境：方向与指引（生活与学习·方向与指引）　|　核心词汇：direction　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 direction 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 the guide ① took a direction that no walker in the valley would have chosen, and he said the taking was the whole of the day. The ② direction, meaning the way and not the instruction, ran sixteen miles and stayed unpainted on the signpost; a direction, he said, is the only thing in a valley that is judged by how long it is left unmarked.

Every ③ direction in that valley had the same turned signpost at the corner of it, and the ④ direction at the end, meaning the one they kept for the winter road and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked about twice. A direction, his nephew said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to ask; the guide said the patience is the part that fills sixteen miles.

The clerk meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the direction was the whole of the letter, meaning the instruction and not the way. The ⑥ direction, meaning the instruction and not any of that, is the only thing in a letter that everybody reads and nobody follows; direction, he said, is either something you take or the only word that means both a way and an instruction. He said the instruction is the part they remember.

By 1956 the ⑦ direction had become a line in a handbook, and the handbook had become an argument about the turned signpost. The ⑧ direction of the whole thing, the guide wrote in September, was one valley and sixteen miles of asking; direction, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to ask. She said the asking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ direction I remember is the one at the end, which was repainted in 1970 and is still described as the strangest in the valley. A ⑩ direction, the nephew said in 1972, is the only thing that improves by being followed; every direction, she said, is an instruction that has agreed to look like a way. She said the instruction was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 方向；方位（指山谷里选的那一条路向）
B. n. 方向（指那条路向本身，与那个指示相对）
C. 固定搭配：take a direction 选取一个方向
D. n. 方向（指留给冬季道路用的那一条）
E. n. 方向；走向（抽象总称，指一条山谷的全部路向）
F. n. 方向（指手册上写到、被标明的那一条）
G. n. 指示；说明（指信里给出的那道吩咐）
H. n. 指示（抽象总称，指人人读到却无人照做的那道）

items.q: took a direction that no walker in the valley would have chosen
The direction, meaning the way and not the instruction
the direction was the whole of the letter
the direction had become a line in a handbook
The direction of the whole thing
A direction, the nephew said in 1972

answers.why: take a direction 意为“选取一个方向”，1947 年向导选了一个山谷里没有一位步行者会选的方向。
direction 意为“方向”，指那条路向本身而不是那个指示，它走了十六英里而路牌上没有漆字。
direction 意为“方向、方位”，指那条山谷里每一个方向，每一个拐角处都有同一块被转过的路牌。
direction 意为“方向”，指留给冬季道路用的那一条，是唯一有人问过两次的。
direction 意为“指示、说明”，指信里给出的那道吩咐，办事员说这道指示就是那封信的全部。
direction 意为“指示”，指人人读到却无人照做的那道而不是那条路向，是信里人人都读到、却无人照做的东西。
direction 意为“方向”，指手册上写到、被标明的那一条，到 1956 年这个方向成了手册里的一行。
direction 意为“方向、走向”，向导九月写道，整件事的走向是一条山谷和十六英里的问路。
direction 意为“方向”，我记得的是末尾那一条，1970 年重新漆过，至今仍被说成山谷里最奇的一条。
direction 为抽象总称，侄子 1972 年说，一个方向是唯一会因为被照着走而变得更好的东西。
